convertibility_reason: Uses two iCustom indicators (JBrainTrend1Sig, UltraRSI) with unknown internals, plus external .mqh includes (SmoothAlgorithms.mqh, TradeAlgorithms.mqh). The signal logic from custom indicators must be manually reimplemented in Python.

derived_values.name: JBrainSig1_direction

derived_values.name: UltraRSI_crossover_up
derived_values.formula: UpVal2[1] > DnVal2[1] AND UpVal2[0] <= DnVal2[0] (buffer 0 crosses above buffer 1)

derived_values.name: UltraRSI_crossover_dn
derived_values.formula: DnVal2[1] > UpVal2[1] AND DnVal2[0] <= UpVal2[0] (buffer 1 crosses above buffer 0)

custom_logic_notes: Three algorithm modes via AlgMode enum: (1) JBrainSig1Filter - UltraRSI provides entry signal, JBrainTrend1Sig acts as filter; (2) UltraRSIFilter - JBrainTrend1Sig provides entry signal, UltraRSI acts as filter; (3) Composition - both indicators must agree. JBrainTrend1Sig uses a backward scan from SignalBar to find the last non-zero direction signal (trend-following, not just current bar). UltraRSI uses crossover of its two buffers (Up line vs Down line). Exit signals in Composition mode require BOTH indicators to confirm close. The JBrainTrend1Sig indicator internally uses ATR(7) and Stochastic(9) with JMA smoothing (XLength=7, XPhase=100). The UltraRSI indicator internally uses RSI(13) with multi-stage JJMA smoothing. The CXMA class from SmoothAlgorithms.mqh calculates min_rates_total. TradeAlgorithms.mqh provides BuyPositionOpen/SellPositionOpen/BuyPositionClose/SellPositionClose and GlobalVariableDel_/CIsNewBar/LoadHistory utilities.
python_conversion_notes: Must reimplement two custom indicators: (1) JBrainTrend1Sig - requires ATR, Stochastic, and JMA smoothing algorithm from SmoothAlgorithms.mqh; the JJMA/JurX/ParMA/T3/VIDYA/AMA smoothing methods are proprietary and must be ported. (2) UltraRSI - requires RSI calculation followed by cascading variable-period JJMA smoothing with nStep=5, nStepsTotal=10. Both indicators are non-trivial to reimplement. Consider using ta-lib for base RSI/ATR/Stochastic, but the JJMA and other exotic smoothers have no Python library equivalents and must be manually translated from SmoothAlgorithms.mqh. The three-mode entry logic (JBrainSig1Filter/UltraRSIFilter/Composition) and the backward-scanning JBrainTrend1Sig direction detection add significant complexity. Start by porting SmoothAlgorithms.mqh smoothing functions to Python as a shared module.
